## Goal

Document the herdr worklist hydrator in packages/herdr/README.md so operators understand its cadence, semantics, safety, and why pane-title IDs must survive truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README documents: 30s cadence, immediate run on focus-resume, visibility gating (zero wl while hidden).
2. README documents demotion rules (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open) with the status/stage compatibility note.
3. README documents fail-open semantics (missing/unparseable CLI output → no demotions, never a crash).
4. README documents the pane-title ID-survival rationale (matching relies on ' - WL-<id>' in titles; pane-title amendment F0).
5. Docs match the shipped implementation (reviewed at close).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/README.md

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a 'Hydrator' subsection under the worklist/downtime worker docs area with the bullets above.

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (implementation facts) and F0 (format rationale)

# Wire up interview command to shortcut chord

## Problem statement

Herdr's `r` key is currently a single-key Producer Review shortcut. Convert it to a prefix key, adding `r-p` (Producer Review) and `r-i` (`wl interview`) as two-key chords — enabling a consistent `r`-prefix axis for work-item review workflows.

## Users

- **Map** (agent operator): Wants faster access to interview mode for work items with outstanding producer review questions, via a consistent `r` prefix axis alongside other work-item management chords (e.g. `a` for audit, `u` for update, `x` for close).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `r` key is converted from a single-key shortcut to a prefix key with two children:
   - `r-p`: Runs Producer Review (the existing single-key command moved to chord)
   - `r-i`: Runs `wl interview <id>` to walk through outstanding interview questions on the selected work item
2. No existing shortcut functionality is lost — Producer Review still works via `r-p`.
3. The shortcut hints in the help line correctly display `r-p: Producer Review` and `r-i: interview` when `r` is pressed as a prefix.
4. All existing shortcut chords (audit `a-*`, update `u-*`, filter `f-*`, etc.) remain unaffected.

5. At least one automated test validates the new `r-p` and `r-i` chords (e.g. a `shortcut-config` unit test asserting both chords resolve to the expected commands).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- This is a configuration-only change in `shortcuts.json`; no code changes needed.
- The chord system already supports multi-key chords (e.g. `a,a`, `u,p,l`), so no changes to `shortcut-config.ts` are required.

## Existing state

- `shortcuts.json` entry for `r`: single-key chord running `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>` (Producer Review).
- The chord system in `shortcut-config.ts` already supports arbitrary-length chords and leader-key prefix lookups via `getChordByLeader()`.

## Desired change

- Replace the single-key `r` entry with two two-key entries:
  - `r-p`: `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>`
  - `r-i`: `!!wl interview <id>`
- Remove `r` as a single-key shortcut.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — chord registry; edit to replace `r` entry with `r-p` and `r-i` entries

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: This is narrowly scoped to shortcuts.json. Adding more `r`-prefix chords (e.g. `r-n` for intake, `r-s` for ship) are out of scope but could be follow-up work items.
- **Breaking change**: The `r` single-key shortcut is removed; users who relied on `r` for quick Producer Review must use `r-p` instead.
- **Assumption**: The chord system's prefix handling in `shortcut-config.ts` already works correctly when a single-key entry is replaced by two-key entries starting with the same key — no code changes needed.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O — Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides
- WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR — Herdr: add/remove/edit inline notes on any markdown document (adds `n-e` and `n-d` chords)

## Clarifying questions and answers

1. Q: Should `r` become a prefix only (removing single-key Producer Review), or use a different prefix key? — A: `r` becomes prefix only (option a). The work item description explicitly states "Make r a prefix key" and "r-p: Move the existing Producer Review command to r chord". Source: work item description + code inspection.
2. Q: Should the interview command be `!!wl interview <id>` (shell) or `/herdr:interview <id>` (agent command)? — A: `!!wl interview <id>`. The interview command is a `wl` subcommand, not a `/herdr:` agent command, so it must be a shell command. Source: `wl --help` inspection.
data.title: Wire up interview command to shortcut chord

## Addendum — this is a **batch** mis-context, not a one-off

Follow-up evidence found while verifying the disposition. Strengthens **Q3**
and raises the urgency of **Q1**: these items are actively consuming agent
slots on work that cannot exist in this repository.

**12 ContextHub items** are `[test-failure] proxy/tests/*` reports. ContextHub
has **never** contained a `proxy/` tree:

- `find . -type d -name proxy` → no match (excluding `node_modules`)
- `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'proxy/*'` → no match (never added, in any
  branch, in this repository's history)
- `proxy/tests/test_hard_routing_cap.py` **is** tracked on llm-manager
  `origin/dev` (`100644 blob 65d524f6…`)

Batch composition (`wl list "proxy/tests"`):

| Status | Count |
|---|---|
| `in-progress` | 5 |
| `open` (`intake_complete`) | 6 |
| `completed` / `done` | 1 |

Batch members:

| Id | Status | Stage |
|---|---|---|
| `WL-0MUK0KBDW002U1TV` (`test_abandoned_future.py`) | completed | done |
| `WL-0MUK0KCMX007YIFF` (`test_backend_resilience.py`) | open | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KDVR009FACK` (`test_cap_persistence_pin.py`) | open | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KF3V00277J3` (`test_clamp_derived_persistence.py`) | open | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KGCM007ZXHE` (`test_hard_routing_cap.py`) — **this item** | open | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KHLJ007HPMR` (`test_local_dispatch_gate.py`) | open | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KIVA0062U6M` (`test_prefill_lease_extension.py`) | in-progress | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KK3A007O8Q4` (`test_provider_per_slot_ctx.py`) | in-progress | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KLBA006RHHC` (`test_qwen3_tokenizer.py`) | in-progress | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KMJS00338J0` (`test_recover_stuck_global_active_queries.py`) | in-progress | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KNUH0052SR4` (`test_slot_persistence_guards.py`) | in-progress | intake_complete |
| `WL-0MUK0KP1C009DTXA` (`test_token_rate_integration.py`) | in-progress | intake_complete |

Two points the producer should note:

1. **Dead waste:** the 5 `in-progress` items are being worked by agents that
   cannot possibly succeed; the 1 `completed`/`done` item
   (`WL-0MUK0KBDW002U1TV`) was closed claiming a fix to a test that does not
   exist here.
2. **Recommendation:** handle the batch as one decision, not twelve. I did
   **not** create a tracking item for this (per producer-input gate), and I
   touched only this item.
